scenario: Sediment-core laboratory analysis reports microplastic fibre density only when it exceeds 2.5 mg/L (analytical detection limit). Reported values show a mean of 3.8 mg/L (σ=0.7 mg/L). Environmental scientists want the true mean fibre density across all sediment-core samples.

data.description: Observed statistics among values exceeding the reporting threshold

values.note: Only observations above the threshold enter the record

question: (a) Assuming microplastic fibre density follows a normal distribution with σ=0.7 mg/L, solve numerically for the true population mean μ satisfying E[X | X > 2.5] = 3.8. (b) What fraction of all microplastic fibre density events lie above the 2.5 mg/L threshold? (c) By how much (in mg/L) does the observed truncated mean overstate the true μ? (d) Explain the inferential risk of using the observed mean directly as an estimate of μ.

ground_truth.explanation: The observed mean 3.8 mg/L is E[X|X>2.5], the expectation of a truncated-normal distribution. Solving μ+σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=3.8 numerically yields μ=3.73944 mg/L. Only 96.2% of all events are recorded; the observed mean overstates the true mean by 0.06056 mg/L. Using the observed mean directly as μ would lead to systematic over-estimation of the severity/magnitude of the process.

naive_answer: The true mean microplastic fibre density is 3.8 mg/L because that is the average of all available measurements.
naive_trap: Only events above 2.5 mg/L are recorded; the observed mean is a conditional expectation E[X|X>2.5], not the population mean. It always exceeds μ whenever the threshold is binding.
reasoning_trace: (1) Define α=(t−μ)/σ where t=2.5, σ=0.7. (2) Truncated-normal expectation: E[X|X>t]=μ+σ·φ(α)/Φ̄(α). (3) Set equal to 3.8 and solve for μ via brentq on [-15.0, 3.7999]. (4) Solution: μ=3.73944 mg/L. (5) Fraction above threshold: Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=Φ̄((2.5−3.73944)/0.7)=0.96169.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 3.8,0.7,2.5
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-25*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=300)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-3.73944)<0.005, f'mu={mu_sol:.5f}'
assert abs(frac-0.96169)<0.005, f'frac={frac:.5f}'
assert mu_sol < obs
assert abs((obs-mu_sol)-0.06056)<0.01
